name: Amaranthus

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny, bracteate, usually greenish flowers. Then inspect leaf nodes for spines, stem hairs, sex distribution, bracts, tepals and mature fruit.
shared_traits: Annual herbs in the six-species learner set, with alternate simple leaves.
Minute flowers in axillary clusters and/or terminal spikes or panicles.
Reproductive structures include bracts, tepals and small one-seeded fruits.
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Do not use green flower color or pigweed habit alone; several species overlap strongly without mature flowers or fruits.

species_comparison_matrix.scleropoides: axillary clusters from base to top
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: terminal staminate spikes, axillary pistillate clusters

species_comparison_matrix.palmeri: dioecious; male and female plants separate
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: staminate upper and pistillate axillary clusters

species_comparison_matrix.palmeri: female bracts 4–6 mm, longer than tepals
species_comparison_matrix.polygonoides: five tepals partly joined at base
species_comparison_matrix.scleropoides: hardened swollen cluster axes; keeled pistillate bracts
species_comparison_matrix.spinosus: paired nodal spines remain best cue

species_key: Paired sharp spines at leaf nodes → A. spinosus.
No spines; low plant with hard swollen axillary cluster axes → A. scleropoides.
No spines; low plant with small congested axillary clusters, without hardened axes → examine A. polygonoides.
Tall plant with conspicuous hairy upper stem and thick inflorescence → A. retroflexus.
Tall nearly glabrous plant; male and female flowers on separate plants; long terminal spikes → A. palmeri.
Glabrous plant with slender interrupted terminal spikes; three tepals and wrinkled indehiscent fruit → A. viridis.
overlap_and_cautions: Young vegetative plants can be impossible to separate confidently.
Terminal spike size changes with maturity and site conditions.
A. palmeri must be checked for dioecy using flowering plants, not assumed from stature.
Bract, tepal and fruit traits require hand-lens or macro photography.
Do not confuse bracts with tepals when counting flower parts.

local_lookalike_routing.group: Other Amaranthus in the source pool
local_lookalike_routing.separate: Check mature female bracts, tepal number, fruit opening and node armature before species assignment.
Look at mealy leaf surfaces, leaf shape, and small flower clusters; use reproductive structure to confirm genus.
Acalypha has distinctive euphorb inflorescences and pistillate bracts, unlike Amaranthus flower clusters.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.role: fruit and tepal macro with scale

targeted_handoffs.request: Verify tepal counts and mature female-bract/utricle key for A. polygonoides versus A. scleropoides before declaring a deterministic pairwise key.
Use canonical species image records to find paired macros of nodes, female bracts, tepals and mature fruits; do not substitute whole-plant glamour shots.

look_here_first: START AT THE LEAF NODE. Paired sharp spines? A. spinosus. No spines? Photograph the upper stem hairs and follow where the flower clusters form (axillary versus terminal). Then inspect a mature female flower for BRACT, TEPAL, and FRUIT differences. A green pigweed silhouette alone is not enough.

visual_lesson.intro: SEE a whole plant, SPOT the leaf node and flower cluster, NAME spine versus flower bract and tepal, then COMPARE multiple exact species at the same scale. Three species are comparison-only nonnatives; do not mistake inclusion in a visual key for project native-range approval.

steps.title: 1 · Locate the paired nodal spines
steps.photo_role: spiny node with petiole and paired thorns
steps.look_for: Two rigid spines at leaf attachment. These are NOT spiny flower bracts.
steps.why_it_matters: Fastest useful separation for A. spinosus.

steps.title: 2 · Compare hairy stems with glabrous stems
steps.photo_role: whole plant and upper stem pubescence comparison
steps.look_for: A. retroflexus often has obvious upper-stem hairs; use a second close macro before relying on this characteristic.
steps.why_it_matters: Stem hair provides an accessible clue after spiny amaranth is excluded.

steps.title: 3 · Look at an extended terminal tassel
steps.look_for: Long inflorescence branches; confirm flower sex and check stiff female bracts rather than treating tassel length as proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Palmer amaranth is dioecious; a vegetative shoot alone cannot prove sex.

steps.title: 4 · Identify a small rounded axillary cluster
steps.look_for: Compact clusters at leaf axils and relatively smaller foliage; immature plants may overlap other species.
steps.why_it_matters: Teaches where the flowers sit before examining tiny tepals.

steps.title: 5 · Compare hardened clustered axes
steps.look_for: The clustered flower-bearing axis becomes thickened and hard; verify from voucher/macro rather than treating whole-voucher image as an anatomical proof.
steps.why_it_matters: The hardest pair against A. polygonoides requires reproductive macro.

steps.title: 6 · Count tepals and inspect mature fruit
steps.look_for: A. viridis generally has three tepals and an indehiscent wrinkled utricle; this inflorescence image does not resolve the fruit microscopically.
steps.why_it_matters: Reproductive structures settle IDs when leaves and habit overlap.

comparison_priority.test: hard swollen floral axes, tepal details and full axillary cluster macros
upper-stem hair, separate male/female flowering plants, female bract length

comparison_priority.pair: A. spinosus vs all remaining species

cautions: Photo references use images already recorded on the six species cards; most are offsite URLs, NOT new locally downloaded assets.
Do not put arrows on a photo until its precise part is independently checked.
A. scleropoides is represented by a provisional voucher/face image with unverified reuse rights; do not republish or imply rights clearance.
Native status is species-specific: palmeri, polygonoides and scleropoides remain PROVISIONAL in the canonical records; other three are comparison nonnatives.
